newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Dec CPI partly fell on lower mortgages.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Dec CPI partly fell on lower mortgages.

text.p: Swedish consumer prices fell 0.2 percent in December 1996 from November, partly because of lower mortgage rates, Sweden's central statistics bureau (SCB) said on Tuesday.
Annualised inflation also landed at minus 0.2 percent, while average 1996 inflation amounted to 0.7 percent.
The monthly change was somewhat higher than expected, as economists polled by Reuters had expected a fall of 0.3 percent in December.
The consumer price index was 254.9 (1980=100) in December and the average for 1996 was 256.0, SCB said.

Lower mortgage rates contributed 0.1 percentage point to the monthly fall, while the remaining 0.1 percentage point decline stemmed from slight price cuts on clothes, shoes and telecoms services, SCB said in a statement.
The annual 0.2 percent price fall derived from lower mortgage rates and lower value added tax (VAT) on food, SCB said.
At the beginning of 1996, VAT on food was lowered by 7.4 percent of the price including VAT.
Since then, food prices have fallen 6.2 percent, lowering the total price level by 0.9 percentage points, the agency said.
Lower mortgage rates have contributed with 1.2 percentage points to the total price fall, but mortgage falls were counterbalanced by other living costs increasing.
In total, living costs affected the total price index level upwards by 0.2 percentage points.
